# 1. Compile-Time IoC (Dependency Injection)

A Rivet app composes plugins at build time. `rivet build` reads the
`[plugins]` section of `rivet.toml`, adds one dependency per plugin to the
generated manifest, and emits one install call per plugin into `main.rs`:

```rust
// Generated by rivet. Do not edit; run `rivet build` again.
let app = Router::new()
    .route("/ping", get(ping));

// Plugin: auth-token
let app = rivet_plugin_auth_token::install(app);
let host = std::env::var("HOST").unwrap_or_else(|_| "127.0.0.1".to_string());
```

The call names the plugin crate, so the compiler resolves the plugin and
inlines the call. The generated app carries no registry, no name table, and
no `dyn` dispatch. The request path costs what the plugin's own code costs
and nothing more.

## The contract

`rivet-plugin-api` is the shared contract crate. It defines one trait and
one composition primitive:

```rust
pub trait Plugin: Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn install(self, router: axum::Router) -> axum::Router;
}

pub fn install<P: Plugin>(router: axum::Router, plugin: P) -> axum::Router;
```

`install` is generic over `P`, which is a concrete type at every call site.
That is what makes the composition compile-time: monomorphization resolves
the plugin before the binary exists, and the compiler reports a missing or
mistyped plugin as a build error, not a startup failure.

A plugin crate exports a unit type `Plugin` that implements the trait and a
free `install` function that routes through the primitive:

```rust
pub struct Plugin;

impl rivet_plugin_api::Plugin for Plugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str { "auth-token" }

    fn install(self, router: axum::Router) -> axum::Router {
        router.merge(router_with(AuthConfig::from_env()))
    }
}

pub fn install(router: axum::Router) -> axum::Router {
    rivet_plugin_api::install(router, Plugin)
}
```

The plugin reads its configuration when `install` runs, which is once, at
startup. A request never reads the environment and never looks the plugin
up. `rivet-plugin-api::install` logs the plugin name at info level after the
merge, so a deployment records what it composed.

## Configure a plugin

Declare plugins in `rivet.toml`:

```toml
[plugins.auth-token]
crate = "rivet-plugin-auth-token"  # optional; defaults to rivet-plugin-<name>
path = "plugins/auth-token"        # optional; relative to the project dir
version = "0.1"                    # used when `path` is absent
```

`rivet add plugin` writes the entry and leaves the rest of the file as it
was, comments included:

```bash
rivet add plugin auth-token --path plugins/auth-token
rivet add plugin audit-log --version 0.3
```

The command is idempotent. It rejects a plugin that sets neither `path` nor
`version` (`E3016`), a path without a `Cargo.toml`, and a `rivet.toml` it
cannot parse (`E3017`) — and it writes nothing when it rejects.

A plugin resolves one of two ways:

- **`path`** — a crate directory in the project. The generated crate
  depends on it as `path = "../<path>"`, because the generated crate lives
  in `<project>/generated`.
- **`version`** — a published crate, named `rivet-plugin-<name>` unless
  `crate` overrides it.

`rivet build` resolves every entry before it writes anything. One
unresolvable plugin stops the build with `E3016` and a `suggested_fix`, so a
half-generated crate never reaches disk.

## Shipped plugin

`examples/basic/plugins/auth-token` is the reference plugin and a workspace
member:

- it reads `RIVET_AUTH_TOKEN` once, at install time;
- it serves `GET /auth/check` with
  `{"authenticated": <bool>, "scheme": "bearer"}`;
- it compares the presented bearer token against the configured one with a
  constant-time comparison, so a wrong token leaks no prefix through timing.

The example project composes it, and the gate builds that crate and curls
the route.

## Scope

The trait composes routes and middleware. IoC beyond that — request-scoped
containers and injected repositories — is not implemented, and the pillar
does not claim it. What exists today is the composition mechanism, the
generated wiring, and one real plugin built on it.
